text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear claim that driverless cars \"are not a good investment\"","quality":"explicit thesis","description":"The essay states a direct, debatable position early so the reader knows exactly what it is arguing."},{"evidence":"multiple body paragraphs on awareness, laziness, control, legality, and liability","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay expands its claim with several distinct reasons instead of repeating the same idea."},{"evidence":"references to blind spots, busy highways, state laws, and accident blame","quality":"supporting detail","description":"The essay backs its points with concrete examples and article-based concerns rather than only general statements."},{"evidence":"counterargument paragraph beginning \"Some people would have to agree...\"","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"The essay acknowledges the opposing view and then explains why it still rejects driverless cars."},{"evidence":"opening about teenagers, freedom, and driving privileges","quality":"organized introduction","description":"The essay begins with a lead-in that frames the topic and sets up the argument before moving into reasons."},{"evidence":"final paragraph restating that driving should always be the same and cars are safer with human control","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay ends by clearly restating its position and giving the argument a sense of closure."}]}
